text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Crown Prince Hassan says that there is a need for a united pan-Arab philosophy.
- Doctors' association threaten escalation in pay dispute if the government does not heed their demands.

- Prime Minister Kabariti says Jordan supports Syria's position demanding an Israeli pullback from the Golan Heights to pre-1967 borders, and expresses hopes that stalled peace talks should not begin all over again.
- Prime Minister Kabariti says in response to reports of maltreatment of Jordanian prisoners in Kuwaiti prisons that the government will "not allow the dignity of any Jordanian to be harmed".
- Electricity board head says that there is no intention to raise electricity prices after last May's hike.
- Doctors accuse their union of embezzlement and wasting the union funds.
- Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu visits Jordan on Wednesday and expected to meet King Hussein.
- Jordan involved in effort to end Sudan crisis, Kabariti says.
- Jordan seeking details of an incident in which a Jordanian corporal was wounded near the the U.N. headquarters in a Serb-held area in Croatia.
